workflow_hypothesis: Tokenizer pointer-index overflow during continued multiline input
pattern: Invalid lexer/tokenizer buffer offsets produce pointer-index overflow
description: Lexer/tokenizer buffer-position arithmetic can form invalid pointer offsets during stateful or continued input processing.
precondition: Valid input is processed through a lexer/tokenizer path that tracks positions across continuation, newline, or buffer-state transitions.
critical_operation: Lexer/tokenizer code adds a calculated offset to a buffer base to obtain a character pointer or indexed position.
interference: Position handling supplies an invalid or overflowing offset to that pointer calculation.
invalid_assumption: The calculated offset is representable and remains within the buffer's valid address range.
failure: Undefined-behavior instrumentation reports pointer-index overflow while processing input, but execution continues successfully.
search_strategy: Inspect lexer and tokenizer pointer arithmetic fed by continuation, newline, or buffer-state variables.
Trace offset provenance across buffer transitions, including signed/unsigned conversions and sentinel values.
Check that derived buffer positions are range-validated before pointer arithmetic or indexing.
Exercise both interactive continued input and lexer-buffer test paths under undefined-behavior instrumentation.

evidence.supports: The report shows pointer-index overflow during valid continued interactive input and later at lexer-buffer locations during a successful test run; both reproduce diagnostics without an interpreter crash.

scope_note: This singleton report supports a lexer/tokenizer buffer-offset pattern. Its reproductions differ in trigger context, so the evidence does not establish that all multiline input or all buffer transitions are affected.
